charts.omitted: {count} points are outside this trace preview.

brand.title: Reading Shells
brand.eyebrow: A little library. An endless sky.
brand.tagline: A cozy adventure in Python & possibility
brand.edition: A story told one shelf at a time
brand.privacy: Your library lives on this device. No accounts. No telemetry.

intro.speaker: Mrs. Quill
intro.nameTitle: And the name on the door?
intro.nameCopy: Every head librarian starts somewhere. Yours starts here.
intro.nameHelp: Up to 24 characters. You can simply be Shelby.

beats.title: Some libraries have foundations.
beats.body: This one has flippers. High above the ordinary world, Atlas carries a library, its readers, and a truly unreasonable number of overdue books.
beats.quote: He has never lost a book. Occasionally a continent.

loading.title: Shelby is opening the library
loading.detail: Your saved books are still here.

desktop.title: A little more room for the library
desktop.body: Reading Shells is best on a desktop or laptop, with a keyboard and a window at least 1024 pixels wide.
desktop.note: Atlas is large. Even by turtle standards.

windows.move: Move window with arrow keys; hold Shift to resize
windows.help: Drag a title bar to move a window. Its handle also works with arrow keys; hold Shift to resize. Closed windows can always be reopened here.
windows.empty: Your desk is clear. Open a window below.

editor.label: Python code editor
editor.filenameHelp: Use a Python module name, such as helpers.py. Import it with import helpers.
editor.filenameError: Choose an unused Python name beginning with a letter or underscore, followed by .py.
editor.imports: Your scripts can import one another. Each run starts with fresh variables.

request.inputs: Already in Python on this shelf
request.inputsNote: Use these names exactly as written. Queue patrons bring different values, so build the answer from the names.
request.ghostNote: A ghost of the answer, for this shelf only.
request.completeNote: Every patron in this queue has their answer.
request.completeLessonNote: Shelby delivered it. On to the next slip.
request.moveDone: Your script matches the answer. Press Run.
request.lessonClick: Click the pulsing grey text in the editor to make it real code.
request.lessonRun: Now press the green Run button. Watch Shelby deliver your answer.
request.lessonWatching: Shelby is running your code. Watch the desk.
request.lessonRetry: Not quite yet. Fix your code, or use the answer below, then press Run.
request.lessonFix: Put the answer in my script

output.emptyTitle: Let’s see what your code does.
output.empty: Run your script. Shelby will act it out, and the exact Python result will appear here.
output.noRows: An empty table — still a table.

queue.intro: A good answer works for the next shelf, too.
queue.empty: Serve the queue to try your code on each patron’s shelf.

replay.label: Replay timeline
replay.idle: Run your code to make a replay.

scratch.intro: A loose leaf for trying ideas on the current shelf.
scratch.label: Scratch Python
scratch.empty: A result will appear after you try an expression.

settings.title: Make yourself at home
settings.openStacksHelp: Unlock the full Python API if you already know your way around. The puzzles stay the same.
settings.resetBody: This resets your current progress. Export your library first if you want to keep it.
settings.audio: Audio starts after your first click, and pauses when the tab is hidden.

saves.title: A bookmark for your library
saves.note: Three local slots, plus a copy you can take with you.
saves.importLabel: Choose a Reading Shells save file
saves.imported: Welcome back. Your library is unpacked.
saves.exported: A copy of your library is ready to keep.
saves.error: That bookmark could not be opened.
saves.sizeError: Choose a save file smaller than 5 MB.
saves.replace: Loading replaces the library currently on your desk. Export it first if you want to keep both.
saves.overwrite: Saving here replaces this slot’s previous bookmark.

commandUnlock.title: New command unlocked
commandUnlock.continue: Got it — add to my Almanac
commandUnlock.bookmark: This explanation stays in your function booklet. Open the book to read it again.

almanac.title: For the curious librarian
almanac.search: Find a tool or a topic
almanac.noPitfalls: The best notes come from trying. Mrs. Quill will collect them here as you learn.

orders.title: Good work, on repeat
orders.intro: Your filed solutions keep helping new patrons.
orders.empty: Complete an eligible request, then file its solution from the request slip.
orders.failure: This order met a shelf it could not handle.

alerts.title: Notes from the library
alerts.quietBody: No loose pages to chase. Your latest library activity will appear here.

tutorial.speaker: A word from Mrs. Quill
tutorial.retry: Not quite. Make the line match “{line}” exactly, then press Run again.

steps.title: First, the question.
steps.body: Every patron brings a request. Read it carefully. Precision is a kindness.

steps.title: Your smallest useful tool.
steps.body: Write Python here, then press Run or Command / Control + Enter. There is no penalty for trying.

steps.title: Keep an eye on the result.
steps.body: Shelby acts out your code in the library. This little window shows exactly what Python returned.

steps.title: A glimpse, if you need one.
steps.body: The blue ghost preview shows the expected answer for this shelf. Other patrons may bring very different shelves.

sandbox.title: Open Stacks · Sandbox
sandbox.intro: A desk for your own questions. Every API and dataset is available here, without grades or rewards. Your notebook is saved separately from campaign scripts.
sandbox.csvNote: CSV files arrive as a table named shelf. All bundled files can also be read with Table.read_table(filename).

credits.title: A library takes a village
credits.body: Reading Shells is an original game about learning to ask better questions with data.
credits.design: Original characters, illustrations, puzzles, and library world.
credits.technology: Built with React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, CodeMirror, Pyodide, NumPy, Zustand, and idb.
credits.api: The table API follows the design of the open-source datascience package. Its implementation here is original.
credits.curriculum: Topics follow the sequence of UC Berkeley’s Data 8. Original lessons and puzzles; no university affiliation or endorsement.
credits.fonts: Set in Fraunces by Undercase Type and IBM Plex Sans & Mono by IBM. Self-hosted under the SIL Open Font License.
credits.thanks: For everyone who has ever got lost in a good book.

error.title: A page came loose
error.body: The library encountered an unexpected problem. Your local bookmarks are not removed.

atlas.title: Atlas of the library
atlas.intro: Every wing you have opened, and every request inside it. Completed requests can be revisited at any time.
atlas.hidden: Finish the request before this one to reveal it.
atlas.openStacks: Open Stacks is on: every request is reachable.
